report:
**Conclusion: Supported.** Abaloparatide reduces new vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, particularly those at high fracture risk.

The strongest evidence is the 18-month, randomized, placebo-controlled ACTIVE trial. Among postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, daily subcutaneous abaloparatide significantly reduced both new vertebral and nonvertebral fractures versus placebo. FDA labeling reports new vertebral fractures in 0.6% of abaloparatide-treated women versus 4.2% with placebo—an absolute reduction of 3.6 percentage points and relative reduction of about 86%.

This supports the claim, but it should not be generalized to every person with low bone density: the approved indication and trial population concern women with established osteoporosis and elevated fracture risk. Treatment selection also needs to weigh contraindications, adverse effects, duration limits, and follow-on osteoporosis therapy with a clinician.
